messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-serving-az11 kvcache-throttle (severity: P1). Links: https://pd.example/INC-2211, runbook: https://wiki.redwood/kvcache-throttle. Metrics: p99 latency > 1200ms, kvcache evictions spiking.

pagerduty: Alert INC-2211 created and notified on-call. Escalation: SRE -> Eng-Infra -> Eng-Runtime.

Priya R: acked. I'm on it — joining in 30s. What's the customer impact?

Mike H: seeing 502s for some legacy streaming endpoints in eu-west-2 hitting AZ11 nodes. Frontend traces show async KV cache misses blowing up downstream.

Sara L: confirmation from observability: eviction rate jumped x30 around 01:12Z across az11 shards. CPU on serving pods stayed normal, but I/O wait on NVMe nodes increased.

Ashok V: @Priya @Mike tagging: this matches the kernel-side firmware patch we rolled last week on az11. Could be interactions with our cache-lru implementation.

Priya R: good catch. I'm running the quick-check script now:
```bash
./tools/kvcache-debug --region az11 --sample 50 --dump-metrics
```
will paste output.

Priya R: dump: top keys show >70% churn, TTLs are fine, but item size distribution changed (many tiny items) — looks like a traffic shift rather than corruption.

Lucy M: Customer reports: two mid-market accounts reported degraded generation latency ~20-30s and occasional failures. Support queue spiked. I've posted banner to status page: "Degraded performance in eu-west (az11)."

Support-Bot: Posted incident notification to customers with code INC-2211.acknowledged.

Mike H: mitigation idea: divert traffic away from az11 for non-critical routes and enable prefix-KV cache fallback for small-response flows. Can we flip routing policy quickly?

Priya R: yes. I'll run a controlled divert to az9 for low-priority routes. Plan: 1) set route weight low-priority: az11->az9 80/20, 2) enable cache-fallback policy (serve from prefix cache if miss), 3) monitor error budget.

Priya R: command I'm about to run:
```json
POST /controlplane/v1/routing/update
{ "region": "eu-west", "policy": "weight_adjust", "weights": {"az11": 20, "az9": 80}, "routes": ["/v1/stream", "/v1/generate-low" ] }
```

Ashok V: I'll prepare a rollback in case this makes latencies worse. Keep canary at 10% for first 3 minutes.

Priya R: divert executed. Canary at 10% for 3m. Monitoring: p99 for affected routes dropped from 1.2s to 420ms in the canary group. Nice.

Mike H: while that's rolling, let's enable temporary eviction-guard knobs on az11 nodes to increase cache headroom:
```bash
for node in $(list az11-nodes); do ssh $node \"echo 0.9 > /sys/kvcache/eviction_threshold\"; done
```
This will reduce eviction aggressiveness.

Sara L: applied eviction-guard to ~60% of az11 fleet. Observability: eviction rate trending downwards, p50/p90 improving. Still seeing intermittent 502s for heavy batch requests.

Priya R: decision: hold divert in place, continue eviction-guard, and spin up 2 extra dedicated serving pools in az9 to take additional throughput. I'll ask infra to prioritize GPU warmups.

Ashok V: infra runbook step initiated: provisioning dedicated pools (dpool-az9-quick) — ETA ~6m for warmup.

Lucy M: raised a post to customer success with list of affected tenants and suggested mitigation steps they can take (reduce concurrency, enable local retries).

pagerduty: INC-2211 escalated to Eng-Runtime (on-call) due to model-serving impact.

Priya R: @Mike @Sara keep an eye on model quality for rerouted requests — az9 uses a slightly different model quantization. We need to monitor regression alerts.

Mike H: noted. I set a temporary eval hook to compare outputs for a small prompt set. No major regressions so far.

Priya R: current status: divert stable, eviction rates down 75%, p99 overall for affected routes at ~350ms for diverted traffic, az11 still warming but improving. No data loss. Customers on premium tier have been notified via account reps.

Ashok V: next actions: 1) complete warmup of az9 pools, 2) finish eviction-guard rollout across az11 if safe, 3) schedule a controlled kernel rollback for a small subset if trend doesn't improve.

Sara L: logging for postmortem saved to /var/log/incidents/INC-2211.tar.gz. I'll start timeline draft and collect runbook steps.

Priya R: reassigning follow-up to Eng-Infra for root cause analysis. I'll keep this thread updated. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2211 status: Mitigated (partial) — on-call acknowledged, actions in progress. Next update due in 30m or on any regression.
